title: Tommy Lyman's superstitions and working seven days at Leslie House
summary: Lyman was a top entertainer, very superstitious, and got union permission for a seven-day week at Leslie House in New York.

story.theme_name: Going west: California and the Los Angeles scene
story.community_name: Going west: moving to and working in California

blocks.x: He had all the answers. He was a top entertainer around the yard. Oh yes, he was marvelous. He was very superstitious. We were working at Leslie House. Now in New York you can't work seven days a week. And he went before the union and he raised so much care and they allowed him. We had to work seven. Why do you want to work seven days? For me. For me. For me.

For me. Well, I got friends coming from Chicago, going to Paris, blah, blah, blah. So I'm the only guy in New York in them days who could work seven days. So we're working at Leslie House. It's called the Blair House now on West 56th Street. Unless they change the name again. Harry K. Thor, what's his name? Harry K. Thor.

He built that building. And about the third night, I don't drink on the job. I'm telling the truth. He wouldn't stand for it. I never did the last one. But I had to go. I'm going around the steps and go do my business. And when I come back, he's coming down the stairs. So, boom!
